name: M. J. Murdock Charitable Trust Environmental Stewardship Strategic Project Grants
summary: Large capacity-building grants (staff and programme expansion or equipment) for Pacific Northwest nonprofits in wildlife and natural-resource protection, applied for through a letter of intent in set submission periods.

geography.label: Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington

eligibility.rule: A 501(c)(3) public charity, federally recognized tribal entity, or qualifying government entity
Have at least three complete years of operating and financial history
Not be a local watershed council
Request staff/program expansion or equipment/technology, not capital
Have a total project budget of at least $200,000
Receive no majority funding or support from commercial gambling revenue

calls.label: 2026 Period 3 (letter of intent)

deadline.text: Oct 15-Nov 11, 2026; all deadlines are 5 PM Pacific Time Zone

calls.note: Letter of intent stage; full application only if the LOI is approved

calls.label: 2027 Period 1 (letter of intent)

deadline.text: Mar 1-Mar 29, 2027; all deadlines are 5 PM Pacific Time Zone

calls.note: Letter of intent stage; full application only if the LOI is approved

applicant_types.quote: Your organization is a 501(c)(3) public charity, a federally recognized tribal entity, or a qualifying government entity such as a university, community college, or medical center.

geography.quote: Your organization is based in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington - or your project has more than 50% impact in this region.

access.quote: If you are within an LOI submission period, the first step is to complete a brief eligibility quiz to confirm that your organization and project are potentially eligible for a strategic project grant.

window.quote: Grant Submission Cycles Note: All deadlines are 5 PM Pacific Time Zone

amount.quote: The minimum grant request amount is $100,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Grantees must be responsible for 50 percent or more of the purchase cost.

effort.quote: complete a brief eligibility quiz to confirm that your organization and project are potentially eligible for a strategic project grant.
Staff will review your documents and request additional information needed via email.
Your program officer will schedule a site visit to discuss project details, leadership, the board, plans for executing and sustaining the project, criteria for success, and more.

eligibility.quote: Your organization is a 501(c)(3) public charity, a federally recognized tribal entity, or a qualifying government entity such as a university, community college, or medical center.
Entities with fewer than three complete years of operating and financial history
Only staff/program expansion or equipment/technology requests are eligible. Capital projects are ineligible.
The Trust only awards grants for projects with a minimum total project budget of $200,000.
Entities that receive a majority of funding and support from commercial gambling revenue (lottery, casino, etc.)

co_finance.quote: Grantees must be responsible for 50 percent or more of the purchase cost.

after_award.quote: Grant Reports (may be titled Progress Report, Conditions Met Report, or Grant Report/Payment Request): Submit the report by the scheduled date to request payment.
Final Report will be added to your grant record after the final payment is made. Due within one year after grant funds have been fully expended.
